title: Months in Covington and Edmund Hall leaving
summary: The band worked five or six months in Covington and nearby towns playing dances; Edmund Hall then left for a job up north.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Now, what, when was it that he went over to play in Covington?

Uh, and Covington, well, you see, we had some jobs around here. We was playing at different halls around here. And, uh, then we, uh, we got a job to go to Covington. All right. So, after we left here and went to Covington, we stayed over in Covington for about, oh, must have been about five or six months. He was playing all around Covington and, uh, Burger Lucy or Beter Springs, you know. And all those surrounding places around there we was playing because Buddy had a nice name and Buddy was a real musician, you know what I mean? He knew what he was doing, you see? Yeah.
Uh-huh. Whereabouts, what sort of things would you play?
Like, uh, we all, we went all the way to Kentwood, Louisiana. We played all up in Kentwood and, uh, you know.
For dances, yeah. Yeah, dance music. That's right.
And, uh, Edmund Hall was the, um, clarinet player. He was, yeah. Now, can you tell me about how it was that he came to leave the band? Because he left the band there, didn't he?

Well, he left the band after we, uh, left from over there and came back here. We were still playing jobs around here and, uh, there's somebody sent for Edmund Hall. Some of them musicians from up the country, you know.
And, uh, he told Buddy that he was going up, you know, going up there and try to make goods, which he did. Yeah.
He went, didn't he go to Florida then? Huh?
He went to Florida. Some place. Maybe after, maybe a bit later.
I don't know exactly where, but I know to some way up north, just where he had went.
